Department Vision and Mission
Vision:
To be recognized center of excellence in Mechanical Engineering education and research, producing competent, ethical, and socially responsible engineers who contribute to sustainable development and technological innovation.
Mission:
To impart quality technical education in mechanical engineering through outcome-based curriculum, state-of-the-art laboratories, and modern pedagogical practices.
To promote innovation, entrepreneurship, and skill development in students by integrating interdisciplinary learning, hands-on training, and startup ecosystem exposure.
To enhance employability and global competence through industry-relevant training, internships, soft skills development, and exposure to emerging technologies such as AI and 3D printing.
To foster ethical values, social responsibility, and professional integrity in students, enabling them to serve society and contribute to national development.
To nurture sustainable engineering practices by focusing on energy efficiency, green technologies, and environmentally conscious design and manufacturing.

Department of Mechanical Engineering
Mechanical Engineering
is a versatile and foundational branch of engineering focused on the design, analysis, manufacturing, and maintenance of mechanical systems. It combines principles from physics, mathematics, and materials science to create and improve devices and processes that move, produce energy, or convert energy into motion. From tiny components to massive machines, mechanical engineering is essential to innovation and technological advancement across countless industries.
Key areas within mechanical engineering include:
Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer:
This area studies the principles of energy conversion and temperature regulation, critical in designing engines, power plants, heating, and cooling systems, and even sustainable energy solutions like solar power systems.
Fluid Mechanics:
Fluid mechanics is concerned with the behavior of fluids (liquids and gases) and their interactions with surfaces. Applications include everything from designing pumps and hydraulic systems to understanding aerodynamics in aircraft and cars.
Mechanics and Materials Science:
Mechanical engineers study materials to understand their strengths, weaknesses, and suitability for various applications. This field includes material selection, stress analysis, and ensuring safety in products and structures.
Robotics and Automation:
Mechanical engineering plays a significant role in robotics, where engineers design, build, and program robots for use in manufacturing, healthcare, exploration, and more. Automation engineering focuses on developing systems to streamline production processes and improve efficiency.
Manufacturing and Production:
This area involves creating efficient processes for producing goods, from planning assembly lines to utilizing advanced manufacturing techniques like 3D printing. Mechanical engineers work to improve product quality while reducing costs and waste.
Automotive and Aerospace Engineering:
Specializing in the design and production of vehicles, from cars to airplanes, mechanical engineers in this field focus on developing efficient, safe, and sustainable modes of transportation.

INFRASTRUCTURE
Metrology Laboratory:
Objectives:
To provide hands-on training in linear, angular, and surface measurement techniques.
To expose students to mechanical, optical, and electronic measuring instruments.
To impart knowledge about tolerances, fits, limits, and geometrical inspection.
Major Equipment and Instruments:
Vernier Calipers and Micrometers (Inside, Outside, Depth)
Dial Indicators and Height Gauges
Sine Bar and Slip Gauges
Toolmakers Microscope
Profile Projector (Optical Comparator)
Bevel Protractor and Angle Gauges
Thread Plug and Ring Gauges
Gear Tooth Vernier Caliper
Surface Roughness Tester (Stylus Type)
Learning Outcomes:
Develop proficiency in precision measurement and inspection techniques.
Understand limits, fits, tolerances, and Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerance (GD&T).
Gain experience in the selection and use of appropriate instruments.
Interpret measurement data for quality assurance and process control.
Machine Tools Laboratory:
Objectives:
To familiarize students with metal cutting operations and machining processes.
To impart skills in operating lathes, milling, drilling, shaping, grinding, and CNC machines.
To understand the principles of tool selection, cutting speed, feed, and depth of cut.
Major Equipment Available:
Centre Lathe Machines – For turning, facing, threading, knurling, and taper operations.
Shaper Machine – For flat surface generation.
Drilling Machine – For precision hole-making.
Surface Grinding Machine – For fine finishing and flat surface grinding.
Tool and Cutter Grinder
Slotting Machine
Learning Outcomes:
Understand the working principles of various machine tools.
Gain proficiency in machining different materials using standard procedures.
Develop awareness of manufacturing tolerances, tool wear, and safety protocols.
Interpret and apply technical drawings in workshop practices.
Heat Transfer Laboratory:
Objectives:
To experimentally determine heat transfer coefficients and thermal conductivities.
To study different modes of heat transfer under steady and unsteady conditions.
To analyze the performance of heat exchangers and cooling systems.
Major Equipment and Apparatus:
Composite Wall Apparatus – To study conduction through series materials.
Lagged Pipe Apparatus – For radial conduction in cylindrical systems.
Pin-Fin Apparatus – For extended surface heat dissipation.
Natural & Forced Convection Setup – To study heat transfer in fluids.
Emissivity Measurement Apparatus – For thermal radiation properties.
Stefan-Boltzmann Apparatus – To validate black body radiation law.
Parallel Flow & Counter Flow Heat Exchanger – For heat exchange efficiency studies.
Thermal Conductivity Setup for Metal Rods & Insulating Materials
Heat Pipe Demonstration Unit
Learning Outcomes:
Understand and apply basic heat transfer laws and correlations.
Develop practical knowledge of thermal system behaviour and measurement.
Analyze the performance of heat transfer equipment using real-time data.
Enhance skills in experimental design, data acquisition, and result interpretation.
